qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Dominant US on-demand local delivery network (~67% market share) demonstrating clear pricing power via take-rate expansion from 11% to over 13.5% through DashPass subscription scale (18M+ members) and high-margin merchant advertising without losing customer volume.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 6 (Cash & Fortress Balance Sheet, REJECT). While DoorDash possesses a dominant US food delivery network effect (~67% market share) and pricing power via take-rate expansion, reported cash flows are an accounting mirage heavily distorted by massive stock-based compensation ($1.10B in FY24, $1.05B in FY25, exceeding cumulative GAAP net income). The company lacks a multi-cycle peak-to-peak earnings track record (GAAP profitable only since FY24) and has taken on $3.3B in debt to fund aggressive cross-border and software acquisitions (Deliveroo, SevenRooms), failing Munger's real cash conversion and balance sheet standards.
qualitative.evidence: FY24 revenue $10.72B (+24%), operating loss $(38)M, GAAP net income $123M, FCF ~$1.8B, SBC $1.10B. FY25 revenue $13.72B (+28%), operating income $723M, GAAP net income $935M, FCF ~$1.8B, SBC $1.05B. Multi-year GAAP net income totals $1.06B against $2.15B in stock-based compensation, meaning real Owner FCF after dilutive employee compensation is negative to negligible. 5-year median GAAP ROIC is ~8.2% (FY25 ROIC ~6.5%), below the 12% hurdle. Balance sheet holds $5.98B in cash and short-term investments against $3.30B in total debt following the $1.2B SevenRooms acquisition and £2.9B ($3.9B) Deliveroo acquisition.

evaluation_metadata.verdict: Rejected – G6 Cash & Fortress Balance Sheet
